manual.title: Amon Ra Redux Developer Manual & Modernization Roadmap
manual.subtitle: Comprehensive engineering specification for patching and modernizing Laura Bow II (SCI 1.1 Floppy)
manual.description: Architecture, decompilation, script patching, narrative coherence, and puzzle fixes based on the SCI 1.1 floppy release.

sections.title: Foundations and Toolchain
sections.description: Base game assets, Wine execution environment, SCI Companion decompilation, and DOSBox-X regression testing.

entries.title: Floppy v1.000 Base Engine Architecture
entries.summary: The DOS floppy v1.000 release serves as the foundational source of truth for all modernizations.
entries.what: Establishes Laura Bow II (Floppy v1.000) as the immutable base game directory. Loose patch files in the directory override compressed archive resources at runtime without corrupting original assets.

how.lead: The SCI 1.1 interpreter loads resources using a two-tier lookup mechanism:
points: The interpreter searches the current directory for loose resource files matching the naming scheme <resourceNumber>.<resourceExt> (e.g., 0.SCR, 13.MSG).
If no loose override exists, the interpreter queries RESOURCE.MAP for the offset and reads from RESOURCE.000.
Original uncompressed brushstroke background pictures and EGA/VGA palettes are preserved directly from the floppy media.

entries.why: The floppy release contains superior uncompressed brushstroke textures on backgrounds (such as the newsroom desk) and cleaner timing logic compared to the CD release. Building modular loose patches guarantees that original assets remain untouched and patches can be cleanly uninstalled or distributed.

entries.title: SCI Companion Execution Under Wine
entries.summary: Win32 SCI Companion runs under Wine to decompile, edit, and recompile SCI 1.1 scripts and message resources.
entries.what: Enables decompilation of compiled bytecodes (.SCR/.HEP) into human-readable SCI Studio / Sierra syntax (.sc), visual editing of message tables (.MSG), room priority boundaries (.PIC), and views (.V56) within Linux.

how.lead: The developer launches SCI Companion via Wine using the pre-compiled binary:
points: Execution command: wine /home/gordonk/PycharmProjects/SCICompanion/Release/SCICompanion.exe LB2/RESOURCE.MAP.
Scripts are decompiled into source/ directories with symbol recovery driven by Decompiler.ini and selector vocabularies.
Recompiled scripts emit paired .SCR (code chunk) and .HEP (heap object definitions) back into the game directory for immediate execution.

entries.why: SCI Companion provides high-level control-flow recovery (reconstructing while loops, if-else branches, and switch-cases) rather than raw assembly disassembly, dramatically reducing reverse-engineering overhead and preventing bytecode syntax bugs.

entries.title: Modular SCI 1.1 Loose Patching Model
entries.summary: Non-destructive drop-in patch architecture replacing only affected scripts and message lumps.
entries.what: Compiles modified scripts and message lumps into individual standalone files in the LB2/ folder rather than repacking RESOURCE.000, enabling rapid iteration and isolated bug verification.
how: Each bug fix targets specific script IDs (e.g., 0.SCR for global kernel logic, 13.SCR for interrogations, 440.SCR for Armor Room).
The compiler emits <id>.SCR, <id>.HEP, and <id>.MSG.
The original SCI interpreter under DOSBox-X loads loose files automatically in priority over RESOURCE.000 contents.
entries.why: Repacking RESOURCE.000 on every iteration risks whole-archive corruption, invalidates offset tables, and complicates git diff tracking. Loose patch distribution is the standard, verified Sierra patch methodology.

entries.title: DOSBox-X Original-Interpreter Regression Testing
entries.summary: Regression testing through Sierra's original DOS SCI interpreter under DOSBox-X.
entries.what: Executes LB2's SCIDHUV interpreter inside DOSBox-X so loose patches are tested in the original game runtime rather than an interpreter reimplementation.
how: Launch command: ./tools/run_dosbox.sh.
The checked-in DOSBox-X configuration mounts LB2 as drive C and launches scidhuv with the project's loose patches active.
Script regression tests use deterministic in-game saves immediately before key branches; a dummy SDL driver provides a non-interactive startup smoke.
entries.why: The original SCI interpreter is the authoritative runtime for patch compatibility. DOSBox-X preserves that execution environment while remaining scriptable enough for startup smoke checks and repeatable manual save-state tests.

sections.title: Phase 1: Critical Stability and UI/UX Overhaul
sections.description: Phase 1 focuses on core user experience improvements: streamlining the cumbersome interrogation interface, restoring unrestricted save/load functionality, expanding minuscule hotspots, fixing the Act 2 About memory bug, and eliminating visual glitches.

entries.title: P1-01: User Interface (UI) Efficiency & Interrogation Streamlining
entries.summary: Reduces interrogation from five clicks down to a context-sensitive double-click or fast-inquiry mode.
entries.what: Streamlines NPC questioning so players no longer need to execute five sequential clicks per inquiry. Clicking an NPC with the notebook directly activates their questioning topic list, and double-clicking re-asks the most recent or primary topic.

how.lead: Refactors event handling across Script 0 (IconBar/Game) and Script 13 (Notebook/Interrogation UI):
points: In the NPC doVerb handler for verb vAsk (Ask), intercept the target actor instance.
If double-click or modifier is detected, repeat last query immediately without opening modal UI.
When opening the notebook, automatically select the target NPC in the character selector tab instead of forcing manual category and person re-selection.
Retain active scroll position and focus on confirm button for keyboard/enter affirmation.

entries.why: Interrogating suspects across Act 2 requires dozens of questions. Requiring 5 clicks per question generates extreme player fatigue. Streamlining interaction keeps the mystery engaging while retaining full notebook depth.

entries.title: P1-02: Save/Load Functionality Across All Screens & Chase Sequence
entries.summary: Re-enables save and load actions on all screens, especially the Act 5 chase sequence.
entries.what: Ensures the Save and Restore game options remain enabled across every room and action sequence in the game, specifically removing arbitrary lockouts during the Act 5 museum chase.
how: Scan room init scripts in rooms 500, 510, 520, and 550 for calls disabling the save icon in theIconBar.
Remove (theIconBar disable: ICON_SAVE ICON_RESTORE) and replace with clean game state serialization.
In chase sequence motion scripts, pause villain pursuit timers while the file-selection save dialog is active so saving does not cause instant death upon restore.
entries.why: The CD version inexplicably disabled the menu in Act 5, punishing players with complete sequence restarts upon death. Restoring save/load gives players the autonomy expected of adventure games.

entries.title: P1-03: Invisible Hotspots & Pixel Hunt Elimination
entries.summary: Expands clickable hitboxes for tiny or obscure items to match visual rendering.
entries.what: Expands the clickable bounding boxes and polygon boundaries for obscure or sub-pixel items, specifically the skeleton key glint on the painting, the intercom buttons, and the poetry book.

how.lead: Modifies feature definitions and onMeCheck polygons in room scripts:
points: Skeleton key glint: In Room 440 (Armor Room), expand feature paintingKey bounding box from 2x2 pixels to a generous 16x16 pixel zone matching the visual glint cel.
Intercom buttons: In Room 400/420, expand button feature rectangular bounds and assign distinct click regions for each button row.
Poetry book: In Room 230 (Office/Library), enlarge the desk book polygon so clicks on the book spine and edges register reliably.

entries.why: Pixel hunting on a 320x200 canvas is tedious and unrewarding. Clues and interactable objects should reward deductive reasoning rather than random cursor clicking across every pixel.

entries.title: P1-04: Memory Check Error on 'About' Screen in Act 2
entries.summary: Repairs memory calculation logic to prevent erroneous out-of-memory warnings in Act 2.
entries.what: Fixes the bug where clicking 'About' in Act 2 displays 'There is not enough memory available right now to show the about screen' despite abundant heap and hunk memory.
how: Inspect aboutCode method in Script 0 (0.SCR) and 0.MSG string 10.
Locate the memory check condition comparing (MemoryInfo FreeHunk) against an inflated threshold constant.
Correct the threshold comparison to reflect true memory requirements, or bypass the check when running under modern interpreters with expanded memory pools.
entries.why: The warning creates false alarm for players, falsely suggesting memory leaks or imminent system crashes when in reality memory is entirely sufficient.

entries.title: P1-05: Graphical & Animation Glitch Corrections
entries.summary: Fixes characters walking through closed doors, sprite scaling jumps, and actor cutscene collisions.
entries.what: Corrects pathfinding and obstacle polygons so Wolf, Olympia, and the Countess do not clip through closed doors; fixes Laura's sprite scaler during the chase and approaching the headdress; eliminates Steve cutscene collision overlap.

how.lead: Applies room geometry and actor priority corrections:
points: Door clipping: In door controller scripts (Room 440, Room 420), dynamically insert obstacle polygons when doors close and remove them only when fully open.

Laura scaling: In chase rooms (Room 520, Room 550) and Egypt gallery (Room 450, Room 480), recalculate (ego setScaler: Scaler maxScale minScale maxVal minVal) parameters to eliminate abrupt sprite size jumps.
Steve cutscene: Adjust actor movement coordinates and setPri priority layers in Script 230 to prevent character models walking through one another.

entries.why: Visual bugs where characters phase through solid oak doors or distort in size break visual immersion and compromise the presentation quality of the game.

entries.title: P1-06: Visual Fidelity & Floppy Art Deco Asset Preservation
entries.summary: Preserves original hand-painted brushstroke artwork from the floppy release.
entries.what: Protects and maintains the original high-resolution brushstroke textures found in floppy release backgrounds (such as the newsroom desk) which were degraded by color reduction in subsequent CD releases.
how: Extract and catalogue original PIC resources from LB2 floppy RESOURCE.000.
Verify that no lossy re-quantization or dither compression is applied to picture palettes or view cels.
Audit background rendering in Room 100/110 (Newsroom) to confirm full preservation of original brush strokes.
entries.why: The hand-painted 256-color art deco aesthetic is a defining artistic achievement of Laura Bow II. Preserving the floppy assets delivers the authentic visual vision of the art director.

sections.title: Phase 2: Narrative Coherence and Dialogue Accessibility
sections.description: Phase 2 ensures narrative continuity: providing secondary notebook entries for missable character names, fixing confrontation timing for the pocket watch, restoring murder reaction dialogues, removing historical anachronisms, and ensuring character consistency.

entries.title: P2-01: Inaccessible Plot Information & Notebook Fallback Triggers
entries.summary: Adds secondary triggers for key suspects (Najir, Miklo, Countess) so missed Act 1 dialogue does not lock out interrogations.
entries.what: Ensures that key suspect names (Najir, Miklo, Countess) are added to Laura's notebook in Act 2 even if the player failed to trigger specific optional conversations in Act 1.
how: At museum benefit check-in (Script 335 / rm335.sc sGiveInvite state 5 and sExitNorth state 3), simulate consulting the guest register and register clues 263..272 (Steve, Ziggy, Heimlich, Yvette, Ernie, Rameses, Countess, Olympia, Tut, Watney) via addCluesCode (Script 21).

In RotundaRgn.sc (Script 93), intercept Look and Talk verbs in doVerb (sel_300:) across all 11 rotunda characters to ensure examining or speaking to any character registers their notebook entry immediately.
Rely on addCluesCode idempotence to guarantee no duplicate notebook entries are ever created.
entries.why: Missing a single optional dialogue branch in Act 1 permanently locked players out of questioning museum guests about key figures in subsequent acts, creating an unfair narrative dead-end.

entries.title: P2-02: Pocket Watch Confrontation Timing & Armor Room Lockout Adjustment
entries.summary: Adjusts item lockout timing so the pocket watch can be retrieved and shown to the Countess in the Armor Room.
entries.what: Revises item pickup availability and rendezvous gating so Laura can obtain the pocket watch in time to confront the Countess during her secret Armor Room meeting with Little/Ziggy.

how.lead: Modifies condition logic in Room 440 (440.SCR, sMeetingNo2) and the watch location script:
points: Remove premature lockout flags preventing the pocket watch from being taken from Carrington's office prior to meeting trigger.
Adjust sMeetingNo2 script timing to allow player entrance with watch in inventory.
In Countess doVerb handler, wire the vWatch case to trigger the dramatic confrontational dialogue branch.

entries.why: The Armor Room confrontation contains crucial narrative revelations, but the original script's strict item availability window made triggering it nearly impossible.

entries.title: P2-03: Murder Reaction Restoration & Text-First Voice Architecture
entries.summary: Restores murder reaction dialogue via text message lumps, omitting insensitive CD voice tracks while preserving hooks for future custom re-recordings.
entries.what: Activates inaccessible dialogue branches in MSG message resources where characters react to discovered murders (O'Reilly discussing Ziggy's or Carrington's death) and death messages. Explicitly omits the culturally insensitive CD voice acting tracks, focusing purely on high-fidelity text while maintaining SCI audio sync hooks for future custom recordings.

how.lead: Synchronizes discovery cutscene flags and interrogation switch dispatchers across MuseumRgn (Script 90), RotundaRgn (Script 93), aHeimlich (Script 32), and aRameses (Script 36):
points: Set narrative homicide flags (171 & 134 in rm630, 143 in rm435, 158 in rm420, 161 in rm500, 165 in rm525, 155 in rm620) upon corpse and clue discovery.
Update suspect interrogation case switches (topics 258, 259, 264, 266, 267, 780) with dual-tier fallback checks against physical discovery flags.
Wire missing topic 269 case in O'Riley (MuseumRgn) to activate authored dialogue sequence 70 for Countess Waldorf-Carlton's murder.
Enable Ziggy's severed head exhibit display in room 490 via dual-tier flag 143/72 check.
Retain SCI talker sync cue hooks in message resources without referencing legacy CD RESOURCE.AUD lumps, allowing new voice files to be dropped in seamlessly later.

entries.why: The original 1993 CD voice performances were widely criticized for insensitive caricatures and uneven delivery. Focusing strictly on text in the floppy release preserves the authentic noir mystery tone while establishing a clean foundation for future voice talent.

entries.title: P2-04: Narrative Anachronisms Review and Historical Correction
entries.summary: Corrects and clarifies suspect references against the game's internally established late-1926 chronology.
entries.what: Corrects dialogue strings against the game's late-1926 chronology: replaces the 1945 Pippi Longstocking reference, distinguishes the experimental 1926 transatlantic radiotelephone exchange from the 1927 commercial service, and identifies Hemingway's The Sun Also Rises as newly published.
how: Override only the affected message modules with LB2/250.MSG, LB2/270.MSG, and LB2/310.MSG, leaving RESOURCE.MSG and the base archives immutable.
In module 270, replace Lo Fat's postwar Pippi Longstocking misunderstanding with Pip from Dickens' Great Expectations and adjust the follow-up line.
In module 250, identify the New York-London exchange as an experimental two-way radiotelephone conversation, accurately distinguishing it from commercial service introduced in 1927.
In module 310, have Laura explicitly identify The Sun Also Rises as Hemingway's newly published novel.
Audit the effective text layer across all 103 message modules so loose overrides are substituted for the corresponding archived modules before checking obsolete strings.
entries.why: The 1926 period setting is central to the game's atmosphere. Following its internal late-year evidence avoids replacing one apparent anachronism with another and preserves a genuine 1926 communications milestone.

entries.title: P2-05: Contextual Dialogue Errors & Premature Familiarity
entries.summary: Routes six museum characters through formal introductions when Laura has not met them.
entries.what: Corrects dialogue routines where Laura speaks as if she already knows Pippin, Dr. Smith, Countess, Yvette, O'Riley, or Rameses before a formal introduction has occurred.
how: Reuse Sierra's existing museum acquaintance flags: Pippin 110, Dr. Smith 111, Countess 112, Yvette 113, O'Riley 114, and Rameses 115.
In actor scripts 35, 36, and 90, route Talk to condition 80 while the corresponding flag is unset; otherwise preserve the existing handler.
Supply loose overrides 1882.MSG, 1883.MSG, and 1888.MSG so Laura opens neutrally and Pippin, Dr. Smith, and O'Riley identify themselves without changing message tuple metadata.
entries.why: Laura demonstrating psychic foreknowledge of suspect identities before meeting them breaks narrative continuity and player agency.

entries.title: P2-06: Steve & Laura Character Consistency & Romance Flagging
entries.summary: Gates Laura's jealousy and Steve's romantic banter behind Act 1 conversation completion.
entries.what: Ensures that Laura's romantic jealousy and Steve's comments about attending the party to see her only trigger if the player actually conversed with Steve in Act 1.
how: Set relationship flag 122 when Laura initiates either Talk or Ask with Steve in Act 1 room Script 240.
In museum Scripts 330, 335, and 350, require flag 122 in addition to the existing timing and presence checks before starting Steve's kiss, embrace, or reunion sequences.
If the flag is unset, preserve ordinary room initialization and the professional coworker flow.
entries.why: If Laura ignored Steve completely during the prologue, sudden intense jealousy at the museum party appears irrational and unmotivated.

entries.title: P2-07: Dagger Discovery Reaction & Inventory Hand-off
entries.summary: Adds meaningful character reactions to seeing the dagger and fixes inventory removal upon giving it to O'Reilly.
entries.what: Characters respond with genuine shock, fear, or suspicion when presented with the actual Dagger of Amon Ra; giving the dagger to Officer O'Reilly correctly removes it from Laura's inventory.

how.lead: Uses the dagger's existing verb 22 and loose resource overrides:
points: Replace the replica and gift-shop responses in modules 1884, 1885, and 1887 through 1892 with tailored recognition of the authentic artifact.
In both O'Reilly actor handlers (Scripts 90 and 93), preserve normal verb-22 dialogue and then execute (gEgo sel_351: 11) when Laura owns the dagger.
Use inventory ownership as the canonical custody state, so the icon disappears immediately without adding a parallel hand-off flag.

entries.why: Finding the titular stolen relic is the central objective of the mystery; suspects ignoring it breaks narrative logic, and retaining the dagger after handing it to police causes item duplication glitches.

entries.title: P2-08: Period Dialogue De-Caricature Pass
entries.summary: Replaces phonetic ethnic caricature with distinct, readable character voices while preserving the 1926 setting and dramatic intent.
entries.what: Rewrites culturally stereotyped dialogue act by act without erasing identity, clues, jokes, period attitudes, or characterization. Act 1 covers Lo Fat, Sgt. O'Flaherty, and Detective O'Riley.

how.lead: Uses reviewed tuple-addressed manifests and loose message overrides:
points: Give Lo Fat polished grammar, dry humour, and a light British-English cadence while retaining his garment knowledge, baseball interest, flirtation, and clue disclosures.
Give Sgt. O'Flaherty readable Irish-American rhythm and idiom without stage-Irish phonetic spelling, while retaining his hunger, obstruction, and speakeasy hint.
Keep O'Riley blustering, sexist, and deliberately theatrical because those qualities serve his antagonistic role, but make every sentence intelligible.
Apply text by exact noun, verb, condition, sequence, and talker tuple with tools/dialogue.py; preserve all routing and reference metadata.

entries.why: Ethnic spelling should not substitute for character. Distinct voices can remain historically grounded and dramatically useful without making cultural identity itself the joke.

sections.title: Phase 3: Gameplay, Puzzles, and Progression Logic Refinement
sections.description: Phase 3 resolves gameplay design flaws: preventing permanent item loss for Act 5 progression, redesigning the snake oil refill system, smoothing act pacing, adding fair warnings before instant death zones, and stabilizing NPC movement.

entries.title: P3-01: Dead Man Walking Prevention (Act 5 Critical Items)
entries.summary: Guarantees items critical for Act 5 survival (Wire Cutters, Snake Oil, Cheese) cannot be permanently missed.
entries.what: Prevents unwinnable game states in Act 5 by repairing missing Wire Cutters, Snake Oil, and Cheese exactly once when the act begins or an older Act 5 save is resumed.

how.lead: Implements a guarded supply audit in Main's room-transition handler:
points: When global123 first equals 5, grant missing inventory indices 10 (Wire Cutters), 14 (Snake Oil), and 16 (Cheese).
If the snake-oil charge counter global150 is empty, restore its four usable charges.
Set unused flag 123 after the audit so later consumption remains permanent while existing Act 5 saves are repaired on their next room initialization.

entries.why: Forcing players into an inescapable death in Act 5 due to an untelegraphed omission in Act 2 or 3 is the worst hallmark of retro adventure design.

entries.title: P3-02: Snake Oil Refill Mechanic & Inventory Feedback Overhaul
entries.summary: Adds clear inventory and toolbar feedback for snake oil state and makes the laboratory refill jar direct, guarded, and easy to target.
entries.what: Revamps the snake oil bottle mechanic: an empty bottle visibly gains a red-X cel in inventory and the toolbar, a full bottle cannot waste jar supply, and the Alcoholic Preservation Laboratory jar refills the bottle in one action through a larger click target.

how.lead: Uses the existing charge counter as the single source of truth across the actual owning resources:
points: A loose View 61 patch adds cel 1 to the inventory and toolbar loops; Script 15 selects original cel 0 while global150 is nonzero and the red-X cel when it reaches zero.
Room 610 rejects refill attempts when the bottle already has four charges or depletion flag 105 marks the jar empty.
A successful refill restores four charges immediately, advances exactly one of the jar's three depletion stages, and uses an enlarged interaction rectangle.
The audited vanilla Room 610 handler has no Grapes prerequisite, so the refill remains independent without inventing new state.

entries.why: The snake oil puzzle was plagued by invisible state changes, arbitrary puzzle coupling, and misleading feedback, turning an essential survival item into an exercise in frustration.

entries.title: P3-03: Pacing & Progression Audit
entries.summary: Corrects the outline's nonexistent 14-eavesdrop Act 2 gate and preserves the authored event-driven progression model.
entries.what: Audits the claimed 14-eavesdropping requirement against the complete source tree. Act transitions already occur through authored story events, while the superficially counter-like global111 is a later cross-room scene scheduler that the clock can advance directly. The existing progression is preserved rather than replaced with an incompatible synthetic knowledge score.

how.lead: Traces the actual act-transition and scene-scheduling paths:
points: Confirm that Script 26 advances acts only when an authored sequence explicitly enters the act-break room.
Trace the Act 2-to-3 transition to Pippin's discovery and report sequence in Room 454, not Room 230 or a clue count.
Audit every global111 reference and retain its ordered Rooms 510, 560, and 630 scene-scheduler meaning for existing saves.
Route the genuine Act 2 pacing concern to P5-01, where new museum activities can be designed after the bug-fix phases against a stable schedule and state model.

entries.why: Implementing the outline literally would solve a mechanic the game does not contain. Reusing global111 as a knowledge score could skip authored scenes and reinterpret saved games, while a second progression system would create conflicting gates.

entries.title: P3-04: Unfair Deaths & Secret Passage Warning Mechanic
entries.summary: Stops Laura safely at the dark eastern-tower stairwell and repeats its existing warning before she can fall.
entries.what: Prevents Script 530's unannounced stairwell death by stopping Laura at the north threshold while the bulb is out, moving her back to safety, and displaying the same treacherous-staircase description exposed by the dark passage's Look handler.
how: In Script 530's room-boundary handler, redirect boundary signal 8 plus blown-bulb flag 32 from sFallStairs to sWarnDarkStairs.
Freeze input, move Laura back to y=165, display existing message tuple noun 11 / verb 1 / condition 2, then restore control.

Preserve item 23, the replacement light bulb, as the intended solution and leave the original lit traversal unchanged; item 15 is not accepted because its timer intentionally disables the lantern below room 730.
entries.why: Sudden untelegraphed insta-deaths violate core adventure game fairness principles, forcing trial-and-error play.

entries.title: P3-05: Act 1 Progression Trigger Simplification
entries.summary: Makes the press pass sufficient to expose the dirty taxi and gown claim ticket in Act 1.
entries.what: Removes the aggregate four-errand gate from Script 250 so acquiring the essential press pass exposes the dirty taxi and its claim ticket without requiring the unrelated docks visit, baseball trade, or Ziggy conversation.
how: Audit Script 22's global124 bits and confirm that press pass, docks, baseball, and Ziggy progress are already stored independently as bits 1, 2, 4, and 8.
Replace Script 250's complete-low-nibble taxi test with the persistent bit-1 press-pass test in the room, trash hotspot class, and corner-trash description.
Preserve the dirty-taxi introduction, claim ticket, Lo Fat gown exchange, dressed taxi Act 1 transition, and all three optional errands.
entries.why: Forcing a hyper-specific, unintuitive sequence of actions in an introductory act creates a poor first impression and frustrates new players before the mystery begins.

entries.title: P3-06: NPC Wander Mechanic Stabilization
entries.summary: Pauses museum NPC travel during dialogue, resumes the same route afterward, and extends O'Reilly's availability in Acts 3 and 4.
entries.what: Stops Script 90 museum actors from wandering off mid-conversation while preserving their scheduled destination; keeps Officer O'Reilly accessible after 10:15 for questioning in Acts 3 and 4.

how.lead: Coordinates Script 90's museum actors, travel controller, message callback, and Script 22 clock event:
points: Route every museum-actor message through a wrapper that locks the selected actor and stops its active mover.
Prevent TravelToRoom from advancing while locked; on dismissal, clear the lock and re-enter its current state so the same fixed or random route resumes.
Skip O'Reilly's 10:15 removal while global123 is Act 3 or Act 4, retaining the original removal behavior in other acts.

entries.why: Having suspects walk away off-screen in the middle of crucial testimony breaks immersion and wastes player time tracking them down again.

sections.title: Phase 4: Mystery, Grading, and Ending Logic
sections.description: Phase 4 fixes the detective grading system and endgame logic: clarifying Wattney Little clues, rewarding logical deduction for planted red herrings, aligning hint book claims with internal code, decoupling quiz answers from dagger ownership, standardizing grading point divisors, and separating required case findings from bonus museum inquiries.

entries.title: P4-01: Mystery Accessibility & Wattney Little Evidence Discovery
entries.summary: Provides clear clues to Wattney Little's role and police file contents without pixel hunting.
entries.what: Makes the existing Room 560 police-file path reveal Watney Little and the file's contents through a prominent environmental interaction rather than a tiny book hotspot.
how: Correct the outline's resource assumptions: Script 560 owns the evidence path, where a special book in the room's bookcase opens the inset containing inventory item 24; Room 420 and Script 13 are not involved.
Expand the special volume's hotspot from 11x15 to 36x38 pixels and let Look, Hand, or Magnifier on the full bookcase open the same inset until the file is acquired.

When the exposed file is inspected, idempotently register Things clue 793 for its contents and People clue 272 for Watney; retain the original Take path as a second registration route and preserve its item and score effects.
entries.why: Watney Little is essential to understanding the full conspiracy. Reusing Sierra's authored inset and canonical clue IDs makes the evidence fair to discover without adding contradictory dialogue or parallel state.

entries.title: P4-02: Evidence Validity, Red Herrings & Inquest Reconciliation
entries.summary: Integrates planted red-herring evidence logically into the inquest without penalizing players.
entries.what: Reconciles three canonical physical-evidence chains at the actual Script 750 inquest: the Ankh medallion, Pippin's appointment notepad, and the bloody high-heel footprint paired with Yvette's shoe. The source audit corrects the outline's mistaken identification of the carbon paper as Yvette's schedule.

how.lead: Records the previously ephemeral footprint in Script 454 and adds a post-question evidence review to Script 750:
points: Opening the footprint inset sets unused, persistent score bit 179 without creating a duplicate inventory object or clue entry.
After question 16, independently recognize Ankh item 20, appointment-notepad item 21, and footprint bit 179 together with shoe item 30.
Explain that each clue contributes timeline or framing evidence rather than proving guilt, and award idempotent insight points through unused bits 180, 181, and 182.

entries.why: Thorough investigation should help the player distinguish planted evidence from a verdict. Reusing canonical item identities and the existing point-bit mechanism preserves save and inventory behavior while making the coroner respond to what Laura actually discovered.

entries.title: P4-03: Hint Book Contradictions & Best Ending Requirement Alignment
entries.summary: Aligns internal ending logic with official hint book criteria and narrative necessity.
entries.what: Aligns Script 750's highest-outcome evidence gate with Sierra's published 13-item checklist instead of vanilla's five-condition subset, while preserving credit for evidence Laura legitimately discovered and no longer carries.

how.lead: Centralizes one best-evidence predicate used by every final-outcome branch:
points: Require the Dagger, Watney's police file, Ankh, red hair, pocket watch, wire cutters, carbon paper, bifocals, Pippin's notepad, Yvette's shoe, garter, grapes, and warthog hair.
Accept dagger acquisition bit 155 after surrender and carbon-paper read bit 170 after the paper is consumed.
Record a Look or Take of the exposed police file with non-scoring bit 183, while retained item 24 also satisfies the requirement.
Leave murder-answer, theft-answer, and final outcome meanings unchanged for P4-04 and P4-06.

entries.why: Vanilla labels five checks as all evidence, but three are progression items, making red hair and bifocals the only meaningful missable gates while eight officially listed objects are ignored. The complete hint-book list makes the best ending reflect the investigation the published guidance asks players to perform.

entries.title: P4-04: Quiz / Dagger Possession Logic Decoupling
entries.summary: Decouples coroner questionnaire results from physical possession of the Dagger of Amon Ra.
entries.what: Fixes the Script 750 outcome bug that falsely claimed Laura lost the Dagger of Amon Ra when she answered theft questions incorrectly, even when she physically retained it or handed it to O'Reilly.

how.lead: Separates quiz feedback from the physical history used by the epilogue:
points: Keep the original four-state quiz result while the coroner evaluates Laura's murder and theft answers.
Treat inventory item 11 or durable acquisition bit 155 as proof that Laura recovered the authentic dagger.
At the epilogue boundary, preserve whether the murder case was solved but replace the theft-answer dimension with physical recovery.
Use the normalized state for newspaper art, outcome routing, and all 19 condition-indexed character cards in Script 785.

entries.why: Questionnaire accuracy should determine the coroner's assessment, not retroactively change whether Laura recovered or surrendered a physical artifact.

entries.title: P4-05: Grading and Scoring System Standardization
entries.summary: Standardizes point divisors across all acts and fixes the false F-grade on game startup.
entries.what: Makes Script 26 grade each act against the cumulative points actually attainable by that break and prevents the ungraded introduction from consuming the first F-band narrator response.

how.lead: Aligns the act-break calculation with the complete point-event audit:
points: Replace vanilla cumulative divisors 5, 12, 43, 58, and 61 with Redux maxima 5, 13, 38, 48, and 51; the extra point from Act 2 onward is P4-02's documented footprint.
Keep the authored F/D/C/B/A boundaries at 0–20, 21–40, 41–60, 61–80, and 81–100 percent.
Skip grade-band selection while global123 is zero so the introduction neither displays nor consumes a grade message.
Treat the three coroner-review awards as post-grade points, producing a final raw maximum of 54 without claiming they were available at the Act 5 break.

entries.why: Vanilla divides perfect Act 3–5 scores by totals the player cannot reach, capping a flawless run at 86%, 81%, and 81%. It also advances the first F-message counter during the ungraded introduction because an unset local percentage reads as zero.

entries.title: P4-06: Non-Essential Quiz Questions Delineation
entries.summary: Labels required case findings separately from outcome-neutral art-theft and High Priest bonus questions.
entries.what: Audits all sixteen questions in the actual Script 750 inquest, labels questions 1 through 11 as required case findings, and isolates the art-theft and High Priest questions 12 through 16 in a bonus state machine that cannot alter either verdict flag.
how: Display a required-case notice before question 1 explaining that questions 1 through 11 determine the coroner's conclusions about the murders and dagger theft.
Move questions 12 through 16 into Script 750's dedicated sBonusQuestions state and display a bonus-museum notice before they begin.
Preserve the original answer menus, feedback, and conditional skips while ensuring the bonus state contains no writes to murder flag local4 or theft-answer flag local5.
entries.why: The optional questions were already outcome-neutral, but sharing one state machine with required theft questions and providing no UI distinction made secondary lore appear capable of lowering Laura's final result.

sections.title: Phase 5: Act 2 Content and Pacing Expansion
sections.description: Post-bugfix content work that adds active museum investigation around Act 2's essential social context.

entries.title: P5-01: Act 2 Interactive Investigation Milestone
entries.summary: Adds compact museum puzzles that route the player naturally through Act 2's essential conversations and eavesdropping.
entries.what: After the core bug-fix roadmap is stable, expands Act 2 with several player-driven investigative activities between its required social beats. The conversations remain available for character voice and vital context, but Laura gains meaningful things to inspect, compare, and deduce instead of moving from one passive dialogue trigger to the next.

how.lead: Begins with a dedicated design and dependency pass before any new script state is added:
points: Map the complete Act 2 room schedule, conversation triggers, clue flags, score events, messages, and transition dependencies.

Select several compact mechanics that reuse museum spaces and props where practical; candidates include exhibit-security inspection, guest-register or staff-route cross-referencing, and artifact-handling observations.
Use the activities to guide the player naturally toward essential conversations and reinforce motives, alibis, and relationships through interaction without deleting authored dialogue.
Specify every new message, resource owner, score award, and state bit before implementation, preserving global111 and the authored act-break path.
Create deterministic DOSBox-X saves for the start, midpoint, and completion paths and verify compatibility with saves made before the expansion.

entries.why: The P3-03 audit showed that Act 2's weakness is experiential rather than a single numeric gate: too much essential context arrives through consecutive dialogue and eavesdropping with too little player agency between scenes.
